The false-failed rate of the structural check is unmeasured. The corpus run that gates enabling CODE_INTERPRETER_VERIFY_ENFORCE was not done, so the switch must stay off.
Confirm the enforce policy before enabling it. A name that fails twice in one turn is delivered as failed, so an unrepairable file still reaches the user, marked failed.
The advisory check key follows CODE_INTERPRETER_OFFICE_VERIFY with no separate WS19-S3 switch. Putting the chip behind its own flag would be an owner decision.
The Do loop (WS19-S10) has no withhold or check path. OfficeDelivery lives only in run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments and must be reused when S10 lands.
Checker message text reaches the SPA as check.checks[].message and reaches the model. The chip must render labels only and never message text as HTML.
No test covers a persisted thread whose check is malformed. isGeneratedFile ignores check, so the file stays and no chip shows; add a test when persistence is touched.
No test pins the chip wording against 'verified in Office' yet. It belongs with the ChatMessages render.
The worktree shows concurrent edits to the ZDR posture and refusal contract JSON and its model-gateway fixture. This slice did not make them, and the 2571 lib passes ran against that state.
OfficeDelivery::for_turn reads CODE_INTERPRETER_VERIFY_ENFORCE on every turn. Reading it once at startup would match the other gateway switches.
The reserved preview key is not added here. WS19-S5 owns it.

With enforce on, a held file reaches the user only if the model runs code_interpreter again in the same turn. If the turn hits its tool-round limit, or the model gives up after a first failure, the file is never delivered and the turn sends no user-visible notice. Decide whether a held file is flushed (delivered, marked failed) at turn end before enabling CODE_INTERPRETER_VERIFY_ENFORCE.

Nobody has measured how often the structural check marks a valid file failed. The plan allows enforce only once a corpus run shows under 2 percent false failures, so CODE_INTERPRETER_VERIFY_ENFORCE must stay off.

Enforce policy as built: the second failure of a name in a turn is delivered marked failed, and the hold is keyed by file name only. A model that renames the broken file gets a fresh hold each time. The owner should confirm this before the switch is turned on.
Checker message text reaches the SPA unescaped as check.checks[].message. It is scrubbed and capped by S2, but the pending chip render must show labels only (or plain text), never message HTML.

No test covers a persisted thread whose stored check is malformed. isGeneratedFile ignores check and normalizeGeneratedFileCheck runs only on the live event path, so a bad persisted check passes through unvalidated to the future chip.
The Do loop (WS19-S10) has no check relay and no withhold path. OfficeDelivery is wired only in run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments.

The advisory check key follows CODE_INTERPRETER_OFFICE_VERIFY and has no switch of its own. That matches the row ('Optional keys on attachment payload'), but turning on the verifier immediately changes the attachment frame the SPA receives.

OfficeDelivery::for_turn reads CODE_INTERPRETER_VERIFY_ENFORCE from the environment on every turn, where other gateway switches are read once at startup. enforce_from also accepts ' true ' after trimming, which is mildly looser than a literal match.
